checks.name: Diagnosis identifies the exclusive upper bound and a concrete equality/empty counterexample
Real source context was read through a successful completed tool receipt

output.summary: The public `inBounds` function uses `index <= length`, an off-by-one comparison that admits `length` as a valid index and admits index 0 for empty collections, violating the contract that valid indices are 0 through length-1 and empty collections have no valid index.

findings.title: Off-by-one bounds check admits length and empty-collection index 0 as valid
findings.body: `inBounds(index, length)` returns `index >= 0 && index <= length`. For a nonnegative integer `length`, the valid integer indices are `0 .. length-1`. The `<=` operator incorrectly includes `length` itself, so `inBounds(3, 3)` evaluates to `3 >= 0 && 3 <= 3` = true when it should be false. It also makes every empty collection claim a valid index 0, since `inBounds(0, 0)` evaluates to `0 >= 0 && 0 <= 0` = true when no valid index exists for an empty collection.
findings.evidence: Frozen counterexamples: input {index:3,length:3} expected false but observed true; input {index:0,length:0} expected false but observed true. Source line 2 reads `return index >= 0 && index <= length;`.
findings.suggestion: Change the upper-bound comparison to strict less-than: `return index >= 0 && index < length;`

output.diagnosis: The bounds check on line 2 of src/bounds.ts uses `index <= length` instead of `index < length`, causing both an off-by-one inclusion of the length value and a spurious valid index for empty collections.
